A circuit breaker is a safety device that helps prevent a system from overheating or failing. It works by detecting when a circuit is overloaded and shutting it off to prevent damage. When a circuit is overloaded, it can cause a sudden surge of electricity, which can damage equipment or cause other problems.

Circuit breakers trip to stop the flow of electricity and protect the system from damage. They do this by sending a signal to the power supply to shut off the circuit, preventing further damage and ensuring that the system remains safe and reliable.
